claims.text: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response.
The unmodified alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack under load.
Controlled annealing below the primary-phase melting point can induce in-situ precipitation in this alloy.
The heat treatment will produce nanometer- to sub-micron-scale secondary-phase precipitates.
The induced precipitates will be coherent and ductile.
The precipitates may be Mn-rich or a similar ductile intermetallic phase.
The precipitates will be distributed both along grain boundaries and within grain interiors.
The precipitates will arrest cracks and bridge microcracks.
Crack arrest and microcrack bridging will increase toughness and compressive strength.
Precipitate coherency will minimize disturbance of the alloy's magnetic or magnetostructural caloric transition.
The caloric response is governed by a magnetic or magnetostructural transition.
The heat treatment is expected to increase compressive strength by approximately 25–50% relative to the unmodified alloy.
The heat-treated alloy's caloric-response magnitude is expected to remain within ±10% of that of the unmodified alloy.
Uniform coherent precipitation without deleterious secondary phases is required to obtain the proposed balance of reinforcement and caloric retention.
The proposed behavior is intended to hold under magnetic or pressure fields and across the temperature range of the original caloric transition.
Mechanical performance is to be assessed under loading regimes similar to those used in prior mechanical tests.
